subject: Follow-up: Model-fit & quantization tradeoffs — next steps

Subject: Thanks — quick recap and next steps (model fit / quantization)

Hi Anita — thanks again for the demo today, appreciate you and Rajesh taking the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Signals from the call: you want ~5–10ms p95 generation latency for short responses (<=128 tokens) and cost to be < $0.002 per 1k tokens if possible. Primary workloads are customer-facing chat and batch summarization.
- Risks called out: strict quality bar for compliance prompts (legal/regulatory language), and limited engineering bandwidth for heavy model tuning.

What we recommend as immediate follow-ups (proposal below):
1) Technical deep-dive w/ Vivek (solutions/benchmarking) to validate model fit on a 1k prompt sample set. (~45min)
2) Provide a targeted prompt set and baseline evals using both AWQ and GPTQ quantizations + an FP8 run so you can compare quality/throughput tradeoffs.
3) Draft a mutual action plan (attached) and a simple pilot SOW covering 4 weeks of evaluation + 2-week production pilot.

Deliverables we will share by Mon: prompt CSV, short AWQ/GPTQ trade-off writeup, and a link to the benchmark results. Can you confirm a good time for the deep-dive next week?

Best,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary. That all looks good. A couple clarifications: 

- The latency target is for our web chat front-end; the nightly batch summarization can tolerate higher latency but needs deterministic cost.
- Compliance prompts are ~2k tokens typically and are very sensitive to hallucination — we’ll want to keep any quality delta under 1–2% measured on your evals.

Yes to the deep-dive — Rajesh and I are available Tue/Wed next week (May 4–5) 10–14 PT. Please add Vivek and your SRE if you need to cover deployment specifics.

Subject: RE: Thanks — quick recap and next steps (model fit / quantization)

Hi Anita — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive and what we’ll bring to the benching session: 

1) Recommended candidate models
- Mistral-7B-v1 (float16 baseline) — best cost/quality for short chat when tuned with Redwood-serving prompts.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (FP16) — stronger on instruction adherence and compliance prompts in our internal evals, slightly higher cost.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (FP16) — strong long-form and summarization; consider for batch summarization if quality is the top priority.

2) Quantization tradeoffs to test (we’ll run these on your 1k-prompt sample):
- AWQ (4-bit per-channel, activation-aware): excellent throughput, often minimal perceptible quality delta on chat-style prompts but can degrade on rare long-tail compliance examples.
- GPTQ (3/4-bit per-tensor, matrix-wise): very fast, sometimes worse on instruction-following; tends to be stable for summarization.
- FP8 (mixed 8-bit float): usually the safest for preserving quality with ~1.5x throughput gains vs FP16 on supported HW.

3) What we’ll deliver in the bench run
- Per-prompt scorecards using your prompt set (accuracy, hallucination flags, toxic/unsafe metrics)
- Token throughput and p95 latency for the 128-token and 2k-token tails
- A side-by-side diff on worst-regression prompts so your reviewers can triage.

Notes/constraints: If you need <1–2% quality delta on compliance prompts, our recommendation is to prioritize FP8 for the compliance path and AWQ for chat path (can route by prompt type). We’ll produce a recommended routing policy as part of the pilot.

I’ll bring a short trade-study PDF (AWQ_vs_GPTQ_tradeoff_summary.pdf) and the prompt set (quant_eval_prompt_set.csv). Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Adding a few engineering notes for the pilot test plan and what we’ll need from FinWave for accurate benchmarking: 

Required from FinWave:
- A 1k sample prompt set (we can also use the attached prompt CSV and you can flag sensitive prompts)
- Representative concurrent QPS (approximate) so we can size batching and shard configs
- Any restricted vocab or blocked-response patterns for compliance evals

Planned bench matrix (we’ll run all combos):
- Models: Mistral-7B, Llama-2-13B-chat, Falcon-40B-instruct
- Quantizations: FP16 baseline, AWQ-4bit, GPTQ-4bit, FP8 (where hardware supports)
- Metrics: p95 latency (@128 & @2048 tokens), tokens/sec, average logprob, ROUGE if applicable, hallucination flag rate, and a per-prompt quality delta column.

Quick implementation detail: AWQ gives the best tokens/sec for 7B-class models on A100/RTX8000-equivalents, but watch the tail cases on 2k-token compliance prompts — we’ll pay special attention to worst-regression prompts and produce mitigations (routing to FP8 or fallbacks).

Next steps: if Tue May 4 11am PT works, we’ll run through the bench requirements and agree on access. I’ve added a short runbook to the Drive link Vivek shared.

Thanks,
Dev Patel

dev@redwood.ai
